transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alice Turner (Redwood AE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Quantive - Head of ML Ops), Raj Patel (Quantive - Eng Manager), Priya Narang (Quantive - Security)
Links shared: Deck - redwood/poc-deck-v3.pdf, Benchmarks spreadsheet - drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/bench-ql, Security package - redwood.com/security/ql-pkg (note: link truncated in transcript)

[00:00] Alice: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check-in. we have 42 minutes, lots to cover but main goals are, you know, onboarding progress, access, and the quick perf review. Ben's going to run through the latest runs.
[00:28] Maya: Thanks Alice, yea, appreciate it. we've got a couple new folks on who are helping with infra, Raj and Priya as you know.
[00:35] Raj: hi all.
[00:44] Ben: cool, I'll start with the perf summary then go into tuning notes. we ran three benchmark suites last night on the dedicated pool you provisioned, using the 13B open checkpoint — excuse me, the 13B quant checkpoint. latency median about 120ms for 128-token prompt, p95 around 420ms which is a hair higher than expected. throughput we saw about 220 tokens/sec on the two-card setup.
[01:12] [murmur / crosstalk]
[01:18] Maya: that p95 seems a bit high for our SLAs, our customer facing pages need p95 < 300ms. but what did you have for batching config?
[01:30] Ben: good call — batching was set to continuous batching with target batch size 8 and a 50ms dispatch delay. we can reduce the delay or lower the max batch to trade cost vs latency. also we noticed KV cache hits were only around 12% — might be due to prompt variability in the sample set.
[01:55] Raj: can you explain the KV cache bit? our engineer trying to tune but not sure it's being leveraged. sometimes the term got transcribed as 'K-V cash' in our notes, so wanted to confirm.
[02:10] Ben: yep, kv cache = key value cache; with highly variable prompts you get fewer prefix hits. we recommended prefix normalization and a short prefix cache TTL. that bumped effective hits in a follow-up run to ~28% which reduced p95 to ~310ms.
[02:35] Priya: quick security question — for the dedicated pool, where will logs land? do you push audit logs to our S3 or do we pull from an API?
[02:48] Alice: good Q. for Dedicated we can stream audit logs to your own S3 or push into your cloud logging via a connector; we also provide an audit log API. we'll include the connector config in the security package.
[03:05] Maya: awesome. access-wise, we tried the service account but ran into an IAM role issue, the agent couldn't assume the role. we raised a ticket last night.
[03:18] Alice: saw that ticket, team is on it; Ben, can you share the exact role policy we need?
[03:25] Ben: sure — I'll paste the minimal trust & permissions in the ticket and also put a snippet in the drive sheet. it's basically: sts:AssumeRole, s3:GetObject for logs, ec2:Describe for the peering step.
[03:40] Raj: ok that helps. one more thing: our workloads have token lengths that vary a lot, we have a long context in some calls 1k-2k tokens, will that change the perf profile?
[03:55] Ben: yes longer seq lengths will increase memory pressure and reduce batch sizes. for 2k sequences we recommend either sharding across multiple workers or using a quantized 4-bit profile; the runtime supports both. note the quantized path may slightly degrade output quality in some edge cases — we documented a small drop in rouge for generation tasks.
[04:25] Maya: is the quantization recommendation automated or manual? we don't want to accidentally degrade quality for important flows.
[04:33] Ben: we recommend starting with a read-only run and compare with your eval set. our Optimize tool can recommend quant profiles per workload; but final decision is manual. we'll share the optimize export.
[04:50] [pause / keyboard sounds]
[05:05] Priya: security checklist — SAML/SSO is critical. we need SAML metadata, SCIM for user sync, and we need to ensure keys are customer-managed if possible. KMS integration?
[05:20] Alice: yes we support SAML and SCIM and customer-managed KMS (via HSM if required). for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS; for Dedicated we offer KMS integration options and we can field HSM requests for enterprise.
[05:40] Priya: and data residency for logs? we need retention control and the ability to purge — it's part of our compliance.
[05:48] Ben: purge and retention settings are configurable per account; we also keep an immutable audit trail for 90 days with optional extended retention as an add-on.
[06:05] Maya: great. back to perf, can you walk through the tuning steps you recommended? we tried one patch but didn't see big wins.
[06:18] Ben: sure: 1) prompt normalization to increase KV hit rate; 2) reduce dispatch delay from 50ms to 20ms for low-latency paths; 3) enable prefix cache for common system prompts; 4) try per-route batching overrides for the high-priority routes. we ran a follow-up with these changes and p95 improved to ~280-300ms on the smaller sample set.
[06:47] Raj: when you say per-route overrides, where do we configure that? is that in the redwood console or infra as code?
[06:55] Ben: both — console for quick toggles, and you can commit overrides in the deployment YAML for reproducibility. we'll share the sample YAML in the drive.
[07:08] Maya: any change to cost profile with the lower dispatch delay?
[07:13] Ben: yes a slight increase in cost because batching efficiency drops; we estimate ~8-12% token cost increase for the latency-focused config. but you can mitigate with prefix caching and model quantization where acceptable.
[07:30] [noise / someone coughing]
[07:40] Alice: quick milestone check: onboarding tasks outstanding are the SAML metadata, the service account role fix, and confirming the peering IPs. who is owning the SAML task on your side?
[07:52] Priya: I'll own SAML and SCIM. aim to get metadata to you by tomorrow EOD.
[07:58] Raj: I'll coordinate with infra to fix the role and confirm peering, target Friday.
[08:05] Maya: one question on dataset handling — are traces and user content ever sent to third party vendors for inference? we need to confirm data stays in our VPC for the POC.
[08:18] Ben: for Dedicated in your VPC, all inference happens in your network; we don't route payloads to third parties. we do collect anonymized telemetry for platform health unless you opt out. we'll note opt-out steps in the security doc.
[08:35] Alice: good call. also wanted to surface an ask from our side: if we run the 24h load test, we'd like your approval to run it against a non-prod bucket and the dedicated pool we set up. Ben will coordinate the window.
[08:50] Maya: yes that's fine; prefer early Sunday morning if possible to avoid user traffic.
[08:58] Ben: noted — I'll propose 0300-0700 PDT Sunday and share the dates.
[09:08] [11:20] Ben: quick note on error patterns — we saw sporadic OOMs during the 2k token runs on single-card configs; they went away after scaling to two cards or enabling offload. recommend enabling nvme offload for the long-seq jobs.
[11:38] Raj: good to know. for production we probably want two cards minimum for the long context flows.
[11:45] Priya: any impact on encryption if we use offload? does data hit disk in plaintext?
[11:54] Ben: offload writes intermediate KV shards encrypted at rest; we support KMS for the disk encryption keys. we'll include config flags in the docs.
[12:12] Maya: what's the path forward if the 24h test shows regressions? do we have rollback options?
[12:20] Alice: yes we can fall back to a hosted model variant or older model weights; we also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies in the console.
[12:34] Raj: can we get a quick checklist of the canary configs? e.g., traffic percentages, ramp times.
[12:40] Ben: absolutely — sample canary YAML will be in the drive along with recommended thresholds.
[12:48] [14:05] Priya: another compliance Q: do you have a current SOC2 Type II report? we need evidence for procurement.
[14:15] Alice: yes we do; I'll attach the latest SOC2 Type II and the pen test summary in the security package. also we can provide a redacted breach history if needed.
[14:33] Maya: perfect.
[14:40] Ben: small note about metrics — your team requested per-token cost breakdown by route; we produced a per-route dashboard but need to map your route names to our internal model routes. can you provide that mapping?
[14:55] Raj: yes will do, sending via the ticket.
[15:02] Maya: any known limitations on model variants? for instance if we fallback to a smaller model during high load, will outputs remain consistent?
[15:12] Ben: fallback to smaller models will have quality delta; we recommend automatic fallback only for non-critical routes. for critical routes use canaries with human review. we'll quantify deltas in the benchmark sheet.
[15:28] [16:00] Alice: time check — ~25 minutes in, let's cover final agreement and next steps.
[16:07] Ben: technical ask: for the 24h run we want a warm cache — can your traffic replay or do you want us to synthesize warm prefixes?
[16:18] Raj: we can do a traffic replay from our staging logs; will need a replay spec from you.
[16:25] Ben: we'll provide a replay spec and a short script to ingest.
[16:32] Maya: one more subtle thing: we have PII-stripped content but need to run an LLM fairness check on sensitive routes. is there a recommended eval harness?
[16:44] Ben: our eval harness supports custom prompt sets and can run A/B against variants. we'll share an eval template and sample metrics (toxicity, hallucination rate).
[17:00] Priya: for procurement timing — we need security review sign-off before we go to purchase. can you indicate expected time to produce security artifacts?
[17:10] Alice: we can deliver the package by Friday (2026-05-15) which includes SOC2, architecture diagrams, and the connector configs.
[17:22] Maya: excellent.
[17:30] Raj: anything on cost? we saw an initial quote but need dedicated pricing for reserve burst capacity.
[17:38] Alice: I'll attach the Dedicated pricing tiers in the doc; for the POC we'll keep the burst config and estimate monthly run costs based on 24h test.
[17:47] [18:40] Ben: last tech note — for the 2k tokens you may want to enable kv prefetching and increase the KV segment size; we'll include recommended flags.
[18:55] Maya: noted.
[19:02] Alice: quick recap: Ben runs 24h load test (target Sunday 03:00 PDT), Ben sends sample YAMLs + replay spec; Alice sends security package and pricing; Quantive (Maya/Priya/Raj) will confirm SAML metadata and service account role. next meeting tentative Monday to review 24h results.
[19:28] Priya: agreed.
[19:34] Maya: thanks everyone.
[19:40] Alice: thanks all, we'll follow up in the ticket and with the drive links.

End of transcript.
